title: Synthesis of Quantum Simulators by Compilation
problem: Existing quantum circuit simulators lack maintainability and extensibility; they often rely on dense tensor operations that waste computational resources on sparsity inherent to quantum gate representations.
motivation: Efficient quantum simulation is critical for developing quantum algorithms and hardware, and automating simulator generation reduces manual effort while enabling targeted optimizations for multi-core and GPU platforms.
method: LFQS introduces a compilation-based framework using an intermediate language to synthesize quantum simulators in C and CUDA. The approach exploits underlying structured sparsity in quantum gate matrix representations, generating efficient code paths that avoid redundant dense tensor operations on sparse data.
key_novelty: Using compilation and sparsity-aware code synthesis to automatically generate efficient quantum simulators that outperform hand-written implementations and dense tensor frameworks.
contributions: A compilation-based framework (LFQS) that synthesizes quantum simulators in C and CUDA from an intermediate language specification
Sparsity-exploitation techniques targeting quantum gate matrix structure
Empirical superiority over Qiskit, Catalyst, QuEST, and NumPy on micro and macro benchmarks

metrics.performance: outperforms Qiskit, Catalyst, QuEST, NumPy on benchmarks

limitations: Specific speedup magnitudes and scalability to large qubit counts not detailed in abstract.
